Bootstrap the stability and informativeness of pathways

Source: R/bootstrap.R
bootstrap_pathways.Rd

bootstrap_pathways() assesses, by resampling sequences, whether each context of a fitted tree is stable and informative: whether a sample of the same size would reproduce it, and whether its departure from the shorter history is reproducible. The procedure extends the edge-level bootstrap of transition network analysis (Saqr et al., 2025) from single transitions to variable-length pathways, and separates pathways that reflect a regularity of the process from those that reflect only the particular sequences that were sampled.

Each iteration resamples whole sequences with replacement (Efron & Tibshirani, 1993) and recounts every pathway of the original tree from raw counts, without smoothing or a minimum count. A pathway is stable when the chosen statistic (its count by default, or the probability of its most likely next state, or its divergence from its parent) stays within consistency_range times the observed value in enough resamples: p_stability is the share of resamples outside that band, counting the observed sample once (\((b + 1) / (iter + 1)\)), and the pathway is stable when it is below 1 - stability_threshold. A pathway is informative when its likelihood-ratio statistic \(G^2\) against its parent context exceeds the chi-square critical value at alpha (\(|A| - 1\) degrees of freedom for alphabet \(A\)) in at least informative_threshold of the resamples. Percentile intervals are reported for the count, the next-state probability, the divergence and \(G^2\).

The two flags are read together. A stable and informative pathway is reproducible and predicts differently from its shorter history; a stable pathway that is not informative recurs but adds nothing to its parent's prediction; an informative pathway that is not stable is distinctive but carried by a subset of sequences; a pathway that is neither is fragile. The result is a transitiontrees_bootstrap object, read with as.data.frame() (one row per pathway) and drawn with plot().

The bootstrap evaluates the pathways of one tree; to choose the depth use tune_tree(), to remove contexts that do not differ from their parent use prune_tree(), and to compare groups use compare_groups().

Usage

bootstrap_pathways(
  tree,
  iter = 1000L,
  stat = c("count", "next_probability", "divergence"),
  consistency_range = c(0.5, 1.5),
  stability_threshold = 0.95,
  informative_threshold = 0.8,
  alpha = 0.05,
  ci_level = 0.05,
  seed = 1L,
  keep_resamples = TRUE,
  progress = FALSE
)

Arguments

tree

An unweighted transitiontrees object that carries its sequences (any tree from context_tree()).

iter

Number of bootstrap resamples. Default 1000.

stat

Statistic used for stability: "count" (default), "next_probability" (probability of the most likely next state) or "divergence" (divergence from the parent context, bits).

consistency_range

Lower and upper multiples of the observed value that bound a consistent resample. Default c(0.5, 1.5).

stability_threshold

A pathway is stable when p_stability < 1 - stability_threshold. Default 0.95.

informative_threshold

A pathway is informative when the share of resamples with a significant \(G^2\) is at least this. Default 0.80.

alpha

Significance level of the \(G^2\) test against the parent context. Default 0.05.

ci_level

Total tail probability of the percentile intervals. Default 0.05 (95% intervals).

seed

Seed for the resampling, or NULL to use the current random-number state. Default 1. A non-NULL seed sets the session's random-number state.

keep_resamples

Keep the per-resample values (default TRUE); needed by as.data.frame(x, what = "resamples") and plot_pathway_resamples(). FALSE saves memory and leaves the summary table unchanged.

progress

Show a progress bar. Default FALSE.

Value

An object of class transitiontrees_bootstrap. as.data.frame(x) (or summary(x)) returns one row per pathway of the original tree, stable and informative pathways first, with columns pathway, depth, count, likely_next, next_probability, divergence (bits), changes_prediction, G2 (NA for the root), p_stability, stability_rate, stable, informative_rate, informative, flip_consistency (share of resamples reproducing changes_prediction), and for each of count, next_probability, divergence and G2 the bootstrap mean_*, sd_*, ci_*_lo and ci_*_hi. as.data.frame(x, what = "resamples") returns the per-resample values; plot() draws the \(G^2\) intervals.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) tree is not a transitiontrees object, or has no pathways.

transitiontrees_weighted_unsupported

(error) the tree was fitted with weights, which resampling would drop.

transitiontrees_no_data

(error) the tree does not carry its sequences.

References

Saqr, M., López-Pernas, S., Törmänen, T., Kaliisa, R., Misiejuk, K., & Tikka, S. (2025). Transition network analysis: A novel framework for modeling, visualizing, and identifying the temporal patterns of learners and learning processes. In Proceedings of the 15th International Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference (LAK '25) (pp. 351-361). doi:10.1145/3706468.3706513

Efron, B., & Tibshirani, R. J. (1993). An Introduction to the Bootstrap. Chapman & Hall/CRC. doi:10.1201/9780429246593

See also

as.data.frame.transitiontrees_bootstrap, plot.transitiontrees_bootstrap and plot_pathway_resamples() for the result; tree_pathways() for the observed pathway table; prune_tree() for significance-based pruning.

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 2)
boot <- bootstrap_pathways(tree, iter = 50)
boot
